title: Prompting for Supervisory Tasks
summary: How to write clear, structured prompts that give AI tools the role, context, task and output format they need, and how to refine prompts until results are dependable.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How to write clear, structured prompts that give AI tools the role, context, task and output format they need, and how to refine prompts until results are dependable.
Learning Objectives: Structure prompts using role, context, task, constraints and format
Refine outputs through iteration, examples and follow-up questions
Build a reusable prompt library for common supervisory tasks
Syllabus: Anatomy of a good prompt and common prompting mistakes
Grounding the tool in source documents rather than its general knowledge
Step-by-step reasoning, checklists and structured outputs
Intended Audience: Supervisors, inspectors, analysts and authorisation staff at all levels of seniority
Policy, enforcement and financial crime staff who review documents, data and correspondence
Team leaders responsible for embedding AI tools safely in their teams' work
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Everyday familiarity with office software is helpful. No prior experience of AI tools or data analysis is required.
Core Reading: FSB, The Use of Supervisory and Regulatory Technology by Authorities and Regulated Institutions (2020)
BIS Financial Stability Institute, Innovative Technology in Financial Supervision (Suptech): The Experience of Early Users (FSI Insights No 9, 2018)
NIST, Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0) (2023)
